ev: اعلم أن حمزة وهشاما كانا يقفان
items.note: A hamza at the end of a word, silent or moving: they soften it on stopping and verify it in connected reading.
items.chapter: باب ذكر مذهب حمزة وهشام في الوقف على الهمزة

items.note: Softening a final hamza: a wāw after a ḍamma, a yāʾ after a kasra, an alif after a fatḥa; rawm and ishmām are not possible on the changed letter.
items.chapter: باب ذكر مذهب حمزة وهشام في الوقف على الهمزة

ev: فإذا سكن ما قبل الهمزة وسهلاها
items.note: A hamza after a silent letter: they throw its vowel onto that letter and drop it when the letter is a root letter that is not an alif (المرء, شيء). After a yāʾ or wāw of madd they change the hamza to it and merge (بريء). After an alif they change it to an alif and shorten, or keep the length, which is preferred and comes from Ḥamza through Khalaf.
items.chapter: باب ذكر مذهب حمزة وهشام في الوقف على الهمزة

items.note: Ḥamza alone softens the middle hamza. A silent middle hamza becomes a pure letter, as in المؤمن and بئر.

A moving middle hamza after a silent letter: the vowel is thrown onto the silent root letter (شيئا), and a weak letter is turned and merged (بريئا); after an alif the hamza is put between the two, and the alif may be lengthened or shortened, the longer being the more regular.

A moving hamza after a moving letter: a yāʾ or wāw when a kasra or ḍamma precedes and the hamza has a fatḥa; otherwise between the hamza and the letter of its vowel. Where the written shape is a yāʾ it becomes a ḍamma-vowelled yāʾ, following the spelling of the text.

ev: واعلم أن جميع ما يسهله حمزة

forms.desc: يراعي فيه خط المصحف دون القياس

items.note: All that Ḥamza softens follows the written text and not analogy.

skipped.why: the teachers of the recitation differ (Abu al-Hasan and Abu al-Fath) about merging the letter that replaces the hamza in ورئيا and تؤوي, and about the vowel of the hāʾ in أنبئهم; no difference among the ten is assigned
the teachers of the recitation differ about softening a hamza after a prefixed letter or in words joined in the writing; no difference among the ten is assigned
